groups.title: Foundations
groups.line: What if the layer under everything were different?

items.name: regel
items.line: code as governed Postgres rows
items.question: What if deploying were a commit, and rolling back were a WHERE clause?
items.body: A Go kernel runs strict-TypeScript apps admitted as content-addressed Postgres rows. Deploy is a commit; rollback is an as-of WHERE clause — and nothing lands unverified.
items.alt: regel — code as governed Postgres rows

items.name: kern
items.line: a homoiconic SaaS substrate
items.question: What if every view, workflow and policy — even an agent's patch — were a versioned row?
items.body: A homoiconic SaaS substrate in Lisp — every view, workflow, policy, and even agent-written patch is a versioned row, evaluated by a tiny kernel.
items.alt: kern — a homoiconic SaaS substrate

items.name: eigen
items.line: local-first hypermedia in one Rust binary
items.question: What if one static binary were the app, the desktop and the API — and PII stayed hidden offline?
items.body: A local-first hypermedia framework for Rust — one static binary is the app, desktop, and API; Postgres holds everything; PII stays hidden offline.
items.alt: eigen — local-first hypermedia in one Rust binary

items.name: taal
items.line: the BEAM, built on Go
items.question: What if you could have Erlang's actors and supervision trees without the Erlang VM?
items.body: A small language for building the BEAM on Go — Erlang-style actors and supervision trees, without the VM.
items.alt: taal — the BEAM, built on Go

items.name: streng
items.line: a closed-world TypeScript
items.question: What if TypeScript came with no supply chain at all — the whole corpus vendored and checked in milliseconds?
items.body: A closed-world TypeScript — all of the corpus, none of the supply chain, checked by a vendored native compiler in milliseconds.
items.alt: streng — a closed-world TypeScript

groups.title: Platforms & frameworks
groups.line: Opinionated ways to build a whole product.

items.name: samen
items.line: a governed B2B-SaaS foundry
items.question: What if the boring 80% of a SaaS product came preset — and you could support tenants without ever seeing their customers?
items.body: A governed B2B-SaaS foundry that presets the boring 80% — identity, CRM, billing, support, and the product UI — as six governed idioms on one Postgres per product. Support your tenants without ever seeing their customers.
items.alt: samen — a governed B2B-SaaS foundry

items.name: tinker
items.line: internal tools on data you can't see
items.question: What if you could build internal tools on personal data nobody can read without a second person's approval?
items.body: An ontology-driven builder in Rust on PostgreSQL 18. Define an object once and get a row-level-secured table, a governed API and an MCP front door for agents. Email and phone are sealed by type in a separate vault: queries see a mask, automations get a key, and a person sees the value only after a second person approves. Erasure is a crypto-shred.
items.alt: tinker — internal tools on data you can't see

items.name: chord
items.line: the omakase full-stack for G#
items.question: What would a G# stack look like if every decision were already made for you?
items.body: The omakase full-stack for G# — every decision made for you, batteries included, one blessed way to do each thing.
items.alt: chord — the omakase full-stack for G#

items.name: fugue
items.line: the Phoenix of G#, on Orleans
items.question: What if an app framework were distributed by default, built on virtual actors?
items.body: The Phoenix of G#, on Orleans — a distributed-by-default app framework built on virtual actors.
items.alt: fugue — the Phoenix of G#, on Orleans

items.name: realbook
items.line: the WordPress of G#, with a gate
items.question: What if content and commerce were governed by admission instead of a plugin free-for-all?
items.body: The WordPress of G#, with a gate — content and commerce, governed by admission instead of a plugin free-for-all.
items.alt: realbook — the WordPress of G#, with a gate

items.name: lui
items.line: layout-first UI with an AI sidecar
items.question: What if you described a screen's intent and the framework composed the layout?
items.body: Layout User Interface — a layout-first UI framework with an AI sidecar that composes screens from intent.
items.alt: lui — layout-first UI with an AI sidecar

items.name: cauldron
items.line: a web framework from zero dependencies
items.question: How much of a modern web stack can one Lisp binary carry with no dependencies at all?
items.body: A whole web framework from zero dependencies in Common Lisp — HTTP server, Postgres wire protocol, crypto, a LiveView-style UI engine, an admin panel, and an agent system — shipped as one SBCL binary. No Quicklisp, no FFI, no C.
items.alt: cauldron — one sealed binary holding a whole web stack, nothing crossing in from outside

items.name: crucible-works
items.line: a business platform built to prove cauldron
items.question: Could a zero-dependency framework carry a real multi-tenant product?
items.body: A multi-tenant business platform built on cauldron to prove it could carry a real product — CRM, CMS, knowledge base, billing, and two agent runtimes on schema-per-tenant Postgres — archived with it once the point was made.
items.alt: crucible-works — tenants standing on their own schema slices of one Postgres, on a cauldron foundation

groups.title: Agent tools
groups.line: Making agents cheaper, better reviewed, and easier to steer.

items.name: baton
items.line: the accountability layer for agent runs
items.question: What if every agent run kept a record — evidence that cites, verdicts per criterion, and gates a person holds?
items.body: A router prompt that turns a fresh session into a multi-agent run with a record: evidence that cites or retracts, verdicts computed per criterion, gates a person holds, and state that outlives the laptop. Three tiers replace six rungs — cheap for what a command can settle, frontier for everything with judgment, a person when frontier has failed twice. One more line, TEAM: github, hands the same run to a team.
items.alt: baton v5 — work routed to three tiers (cheap, frontier, a person) while every step lands in a record of evidence, verdicts and gates

items.name: luminaryTeam
items.line: a 40-expert adversarial review
items.question: What would 40 domain experts find if they reviewed your plan before launch?
items.body: A multi-agent technical review framework — drop in a codebase, spec, or launch plan and get an adversarial audit from 40 domain experts across 7 phases, synthesized into ranked fixes.
items.alt: luminaryTeam — a 40-expert adversarial review

items.name: senkani
items.line: token compression for coding agents
items.question: How many tokens could a coding agent skip if every read were compressed before it arrived?
items.body: Token compression for AI coding agents — a native macOS binary that compresses every file read and filters shell output from a local index before a token reaches Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP agent.
items.alt: senkani — token compression for coding agents

items.name: workflowForge
items.line: paste a workflow, get a page you can send
items.question: What if any workflow could become a diagram you can send — one where no two lines ever cross?
items.body: Paste a workflow, get a page you can send. Whatever model you already use writes the JSON; one self-contained HTML file draws it as a DRAKON-style diagram — happy path down the left, exceptions fanning right, severity by shape, and no two lines ever cross. Every step carries a verified, disputed, or unverified state only a human can advance, and the page never reads your process.
items.alt: workflowForge — a DRAKON-style workflow diagram rendered as one sendable page

groups.title: Products
groups.line: Built to be used — by someone, this week.

items.name: aiCRO
items.line: a full growth engagement from one URL
items.question: What if one URL were enough for a whole growth engagement — analysis, positioning, a rebuilt site and a GTM kit?
items.body: A full growth engagement from one URL — analysis, positioning, a rebuilt site inside a guided preview, and a GTM kit per customer group. Evidence-graded and self-contained: it opens from a file, no server, no AI slop.
items.alt: aiCRO — a full growth engagement from one URL

items.name: terminalHelper
items.line: a searchable terminal command reference
items.question: What if your terminal had a browsable library of every command you've ever needed?
items.body: A searchable, browsable command reference for your terminal — a Miller-column TUI, full-text search, and an ask-Claude escape hatch that saves answers to your library.
items.alt: terminalHelper — a searchable terminal command reference

items.name: nonprofitEventPlanner
items.line: run a whole youth trip from your phone
items.question: What if one volunteer could run an entire youth trip from their phone?
items.body: One place for a volunteer to run a whole youth trip — rooming, chaperones, money tracked (not chased), and parents onboarded by magic link.
items.alt: nonprofitEventPlanner — run a whole youth trip from your phone

items.name: customCMS
items.line: one brain, many book storefronts
items.question: What if one local brain could research, write and run a dozen niche book sites at zero marginal cost?
items.body: BookEngine — one local brain that researches, writes, compiles, and runs many niche book-review sites on cheap VPSes, driven by Claude at zero marginal cost.
items.alt: customCMS — one brain, many book storefronts

groups.title: Field reports
groups.line: Long-form notes from building with AI — curve and all.

items.name: bocht
items.line: a whole backend in one Bend binary
items.question: Can an AI build a whole backend in Bend — and prove every claim it makes?
items.body: Bend series, part 1. A whole backend (HTTP, auth, rate limits, WAL storage, REST and MCP) written as one Bend program by an AI app builder, shipped with an evidence discipline worth stealing: no claim without a re-derivable result.
items.alt: bocht: the whole backend as one 1.70 MB arm64 binary

items.name: bochtCMS
items.line: an MCP-only CMS, and the curve its tests missed
items.question: What does a passing test suite miss when a CMS freezes on a long post?
items.body: Bend series, part 2. A blog CMS on bocht whose only interface is seven MCP tools. Its 43 tests passed on every version, including the one that froze for two minutes on a long post. One function fixed: 1,200× faster, same bytes out.
items.alt: bochtCMS: time to save one post bending upward with size before the fix, flat after it

items.name: shellOS
items.line: a desktop shell drawn in pure Bend
items.question: Can a desktop shell drawn pixel by pixel in Bend move from Linux to macOS without changing the app?
items.body: Bend series, part 3. A single-window desktop shell drawn pixel by pixel in pure Bend (terminal over a real PTY, reader, palette), ported from a Linux VM to macOS with no app changes, three screen-only bugs fixed, then redesigned.
items.alt: shellOS after the redesign: panes for themes, saved articles, items, the reader and a live terminal

groups.title: Design studies
groups.line: Designs taken far enough to argue with.

items.name: Overlook
items.line: an open letter to Slack
items.question: What if supervising ten agents felt as calm as reading one channel?
items.body: An open letter to Slack, with the product built first. Columns instead of tabs, a room per project, humans and agents on one roster, and two signals — new, and needs you. Underneath, a graph that can recall what a wrong fact touched, fork a decision into its futures, and blame any line.
items.alt: Overlook — supervising ten agents should feel as calm as reading one channel

items.name: wijzer
items.line: an open letter to Apple
items.question: What if your watch showed how much of the day is still yours?
items.body: A watch face that draws your calendar and your sky on one 24-hour dial — meetings as arcs, the sun, moon and tide resting at their true hours. Three faces, prototyped in HTML at true widget scale, with the ephemeris computed rather than invented. Written up as an open letter to Apple, because watchOS does not open the face.
items.alt: wijzer — a 24-hour almanac watch face

items.name: uiExplorer
items.line: the UI Lab
items.question: What if every interface experiment documented its own making — prompt, model, agents and lineage?
items.body: The UI Lab — a forkable, zero-dependency framework where every interface experiment is pure HTML/CSS and documents its own making: prompt, model, agents, version lineage.
items.alt: uiExplorer — the UI Lab

items.name: omegaClass
items.line: an outdoor fire station in one cabinet
items.question: Can one stainless cabinet hold a parrilla, a smoker and a prep station — and let two pitmasters work at once?
items.body: One wide sealed stainless cabinet that opens into a full outdoor fire station in three zones: a prep + sink counter, a brasero-fed Argentine parrilla, and a vertical rack smoker — sheltered by two lift-up roofs. Designed so a master asador and a master pitmaster can both work it at once. Configure it live, then read the full plan.
items.alt: omegaClass — a stainless grill that deploys a sheltered fire station

items.name: STOWORK
items.line: a carry-on that becomes a workstation
items.question: Can a carry-on unfold into a three-monitor studio in under two minutes?
items.body: A carry-on that unfolds into a full three-monitor workstation — broadcast-grade AV and a swappable compute bay for your own Mac mini or Studio — in under two minutes.
items.alt: STOWORK — a carry-on that becomes a workstation
